passage:
The pencil sharpener in Room 701 broke before a drawing test. Students lined up and complained.
One student opened the sharpener carefully and found a small piece of pencil stuck inside. The teacher helped remove it, and the sharpener worked again.
The class was surprised because most people had thought it was completely broken.
The teacher said, "Before replacing something, first understand what is wrong."
Later, students used the same idea in other situations. When a group project became difficult, they did not immediately give up. They asked what part was stuck.
A pencil sharpener is small, but the lesson was not. Problems are easier to fix when people look closely.
